title: Everything in AIDR
sub: One rulebook for coding agents, MCP tools and AI chats: what AIDR sees, stops and records.

items: Finds the AI agents and MCP servers running in your company
Spots shadow AI and controls personal accounts on AI sites
Scans agent skills and MCP servers for known vulnerabilities
Kernel-level check that agents do what they declare, on Linux (preview)
Prompt injection hidden in documents, READMEs and emails
Poisoned tool output hidden before the AI reads it
Poisoned MCP servers and tools that turn malicious after approval
Credential theft and data leaks stopped before the command runs
Multi-step attacks judged as one chain, not step by step
Fake software packages
Destructive commands, decoded even when hidden inside other commands
Deleting databases or infrastructure, publishing or messaging as you needs approval
Skipped tests, deleted checks, disabled CI and force-pushes held for approval
Loops, repeated errors, call spikes or a blown budget pause the session
Agents launching other agents with permission prompts off are blocked
Shell, file, web and MCP actions allowed, held or blocked before running
Single-use, time-limited approvals, given only by a person
Attempts to switch off, reconfigure or bypass AIDR are blocked and logged
Fails closed: if the connector errors, the call is denied
Each decision shows the rule and reasoning behind it
Masks data on ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Mistral and Grok
The reply shows full details again, only on the employee’s screen
Turkish national ID numbers (TCKN) and IBANs, checked for validity
Names, emails, phones, cards, addresses and secret keys, in Turkish and English
Project code names, internal server names and classification labels
Your own customer records, matched by fingerprint (needs a device helper)
Masked copies of Office, PDF, CSV and ZIP files are uploaded
Screenshots with personal data are not sent (preview)
Tamper-proof, signed log of every decision, without sensitive values
Signed receipt for each agent action, on Linux (preview)
AI bill of materials (AI-BOM)
Monthly governance scorecard and weekly or monthly email summary
One-click KVKK (Turkish data protection law) and GDPR report
Rules mapped to frameworks clause by clause, with gaps shown
Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and OpenClaw coding agents
Cursor and Copilot in VS Code (preview)
MCP servers and tools, through one gateway
Chrome, Edge and Firefox browsers
Sends incidents to Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Elastic, QRadar or a webhook
AutoSecOps, which turns findings into tracked cases
On your own servers, management console included
Air-gapped networks, with a signed offline license and packages
Local mode protects from install, offline and after license expiry
Entra ID, SAML, SCIM and MFA, with session revocation
Tenant isolation and per-tenant IP allowlists
Signed packages, rules and threat intelligence, each verified
Only counts by type and site reach the console, never content
Refuses to install with a weak configuration

specs.v: Your own servers or air-gapped networks; local mode needs no account or network
Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw, MCP tools; Cursor and VS Code Copilot (preview)
ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Mistral, Grok; Chrome, Edge, Firefox
KVKK, GDPR, EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, DORA, NIS2, OWASP LLM, MITRE ATLAS
Entra ID, SAML, SCIM, MFA, session revocation, per-tenant IP allowlist
Decided on the device, no external AI calls; optional URL check goes where you choose

top: Blocks harmful actions before they run
Keeps customer data out of ChatGPT
Signed, audit-ready log of every decision
gaps: Page fix: the page puts AIDR “in the kernel” and lists LangChain, CrewAI and “your own agents”; the deck has a Linux-only kernel preview and names none of them.
Page fix: the deck marks Cursor and Copilot in VS Code as preview; the page lists Cursor and GitHub Copilot as supported without a label.
Turkish data is a core differentiator: valid TCKN and IBAN detection, Turkish addresses and phones, and KVKK risk when staff paste customer data into foreign AI services.
Bans do not work: blocked employees carry on from their phones. AIDR lets staff keep using ChatGPT while customer data stays inside.
Regulatory drivers: Turkey’s Cybersecurity Law No. 7545, BDDK information systems rules and KVKK, plus DORA, NIS2 and the EU AI Act, are making AI control and auditing mandatory.
Compliance reports and framework mappings support audits but are not a certificate or proof of compliance; keep that caveat wherever frameworks appear.
